faq.a: No - EVAP faults do not affect running conditions directly.

faq.q: Is a saddle tank harder?
faq.a: Yes - access to FTP sensor can require tank drop on some vehicles.

title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Circuit High
shortDescription: FTP/EVAP pressure sensor circuit voltage reads high.
fullDescription:
Companion to P2454; indicates the sensor signal is above maximum expected voltage - typically an open ground or failed sensor.

Check sensor ground and replace sensor if signal is faulty.
safetyImpact: Emissions-only impact.

fixSteps.title: Check Ground
fixSteps.instruction: Verify sensor ground integrity.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if ground ok.

faq.q: Can aftermarket FTP sensors cause this?
faq.a: Yes - OEM is recommended.

faq.q: Does a full fuel tank trigger this?
faq.a: No - the sensor operates in a low pressure range.

title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Intermittent
shortDescription: The EVAP pressure sensor signal has intermittent dropouts.
fullDescription:
P2456 is set when the FTP/EVAP pressure sensor signal briefly drops out or becomes erratic. Loose connectors, vibration, or a failing sensor are common causes.

Diagnose with a wiggle test on the harness while watching live data.
safetyImpact: Emissions-only; intermittent code may take time to recur.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle Test
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle the harness while monitoring FTP data.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pins
fixSteps.instruction: Look for pushed-back or corroded pins.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new FTP sensor.

faq.q: Why intermittent is hard to find?
faq.a: Because the fault must occur while you're monitoring - wiggle tests speed it up.

faq.q: Is the sensor inside the tank?
faq.a: On many vehicles, yes - replacement requires care.

title: Evaporative Emission System Recirculation Valve Stuck Open
shortDescription: EVAP recirculation valve is stuck in the open position.
fullDescription:
Some EVAP systems use a recirculation valve to redirect vapors during refueling. When it fails to close, refueling dispense rates and emissions are affected. P2457 is set after the PCM commands closed and sees no flow change.

Replace valve to resolve.
safetyImpact: Emissions issue; possible slow fueling at pump.

fixSteps.title: Command Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Verify actuation via scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install new valve assembly.

faq.q: Is this why my car won't take fuel fast?
faq.a: Sometimes - a stuck EVAP valve can slow pump dispense.

faq.q: Can I keep driving?
faq.a: Yes, but refueling may be slow.

title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Duration
shortDescription: The EVAP system purge duration is outside expected parameters.
fullDescription:
P2458 is set when the PCM sees purge operation either too short or too long vs calibrated duration. This points to a control issue with the purge solenoid, canister, or vent valve.

The underlying cause must be addressed to clear the code - clearing alone will not work.
safetyImpact: Emissions only; no drivability impact.

fixSteps.title: Monitor Purge
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to monitor purge duty cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Canister
fixSteps.instruction: Check canister for fuel saturation.

fixSteps.title: Replace Components
fixSteps.instruction: Address faulty purge/vent valve or canister.

faq.q: Can I fix this by fueling less full?
faq.a: Rarely - the underlying component still needs repair.

faq.q: Is the canister expensive?
faq.a: OEM canisters can be $150-$400.

title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Frequency
shortDescription: EVAP purge is occurring more or less frequently than calibrated.
fullDescription:
P2459 indicates the PCM is not able to schedule EVAP purge at the expected intervals. Reasons include excess vapor generation, valve faults, or sensor miscalibration.

Set by the PCM's self-diagnostic EVAP monitor.
safetyImpact: Emissions-only impact.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose EVAP
fixSteps.instruction: Review all EVAP monitor data and codes.

fixSteps.title: Replace Canister
fixSteps.instruction: Install new canister if saturated.

faq.q: Can overfilling fuel cause this?
faq.a: Yes - fuel liquid entering the canister ruins it.

faq.q: Is DIY replacement practical?
faq.a: On some vehicles yes; on others the canister is near the tank.

title: Generator Lamp L Terminal Circuit High
shortDescription: The alternator indicator lamp (L terminal) circuit voltage is higher than expected.
fullDescription:
P2501 indicates the PCM sees the L terminal of the alternator at an unexpectedly high voltage, suggesting the lamp circuit is open or the alternator regulator is signaling a fault.

Charging system diagnosis with a load tester is the first step.
safetyImpact: Battery may eventually discharge; reduced electrical performance.

fixSteps.title: Check Charging
fixSteps.instruction: Measure battery voltage running - should be 13.5-14.7V.

fixSteps.title: Check L Wire
fixSteps.instruction: Probe L terminal wiring for continuity to cluster.

fixSteps.title: Replace Alternator
fixSteps.instruction: Install rebuilt / new alternator if regulator faulty.

faq.q: Is battery light related?
faq.a: Yes, it's tied to the L terminal.

faq.q: Can a weak battery cause this?
faq.a: Not typically - this is an alternator-side issue.

title: Charging System Voltage
shortDescription: The charging system voltage is outside the normal operating range.
fullDescription:
P2502 is set when the PCM measures system voltage that is either too low (under 12V running) or too high (over 15V) for extended periods. Root causes include alternator, voltage regulator, battery, or wiring issues.

A charging system test is essential for diagnosis.
safetyImpact: Battery drain, dead battery, or damage to electronics from over-voltage.

fixSteps.title: Voltage Test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage at battery, engine running, at idle and 2000 RPM.

fixSteps.title: Load Test
fixSteps.instruction: Load test the battery and charging system.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Replace alternator, battery, or repair wiring per findings.

faq.q: Will my car run with a bad alternator?
faq.a: Only until the battery drains - usually less than an hour.

faq.q: Is high voltage dangerous?
faq.a: Yes, it can damage the PCM and other electronics.

title: Charging System Voltage Low
shortDescription: Measured charging system voltage is below calibrated threshold.
fullDescription:
P2504 means the PCM sees system voltage under the lower limit. This usually indicates an alternator or voltage regulator problem, but can also be a bad battery or ground.

Do a full charging system test to pinpoint the component.
safetyImpact: Battery drain leading to stall; loss of electrical systems.

fixSteps.title: Check Belt
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect drive belt tension and condition.

fixSteps.title: Voltage Test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage under load.

fixSteps.title: Replace Alternator
fixSteps.instruction: Install new alternator if output is low.

faq.q: Is a serpentine belt related?
faq.a: Yes - a loose belt means the alternator can't spin fully under load.

faq.q: How do I test grounds?
faq.a: Voltage drop test across each ground strap.

title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal
shortDescription: The PCM is detecting an issue with its main power input signal.
fullDescription:
P2505 indicates the PCM sees irregular or incorrect B+ input voltage. This can be a wiring issue, battery issue, or an internal PCM fault affecting how it monitors its own supply.

Check battery, main power fuses, and ground integrity before condemning the PCM.
safetyImpact: PCM may reset intermittently; vehicle may stall or not start.

fixSteps.title: Battery Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Clean and tighten battery terminals.

fixSteps.title: Check Fuses
fixSteps.instruction: Verify all PCM-related fuses and relays.

fixSteps.title: Voltage Drop
fixSteps.instruction: Perform voltage drop tests on PCM power and ground.

faq.q: Can a bad battery cause this?
faq.a: Absolutely - it's the first thing to check.

faq.q: Is PCM replacement common?
faq.a: No - wiring/battery are usually at fault.

title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Range/Performance
shortDescription: The PCM power input signal is outside its expected range.
fullDescription:
P2506 is a performance fault on the main PCM power input, meaning the voltage is present but abnormal - too much ripple, unstable, or out of range. Often relates to a failing alternator with diode issues or a degraded battery.

Test charging system for AC ripple as part of diagnosis.
safetyImpact: Erratic PCM behavior; possible misfires or false codes.

fixSteps.title: AC Ripple Test
fixSteps.instruction: Use DMM in AC mode at battery - should be under 0.1V.

fixSteps.title: Replace Alternator
fixSteps.instruction: If ripple is high, install new alternator.

faq.q: What is AC ripple?
faq.a: Leaky alternator diodes let AC bleed through to the DC system.

faq.q: Can a new battery mask this?
faq.a: Temporarily - but the alternator is likely the root cause.

title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Low
shortDescription: The PCM main power input voltage is too low.
fullDescription:
P2507 indicates the PCM's main B+ reference is below calibrated minimum, commonly during cranking or at idle. Causes include weak battery, failing alternator, or resistance in power feed.

Immediate attention is warranted as intermittent operation can cause safety issues.
safetyImpact: Stalling, hard start, or loss of key systems.

fixSteps.title: Check Battery
fixSteps.instruction: Load test battery.

fixSteps.title: Measure Power Feed
fixSteps.instruction: Check voltage at PCM main power pin.

fixSteps.title: Repair Feed
fixSteps.instruction: Replace corroded main power cable or battery as needed.

faq.q: Is jumper cable charging okay?
faq.a: Only as a temporary measure - fix the root cause.

faq.q: Why does it appear only when cold?
faq.a: Battery cold cranking capacity drops and exposes weak cells.

title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal High
shortDescription: PCM main power input voltage is higher than expected.
fullDescription:
P2508 is set when the PCM detects over-voltage on its main B+ input. Typically caused by a faulty voltage regulator or alternator delivering over 15V, putting the PCM at risk of damage.

Immediate diagnosis is important to prevent electronics damage.
safetyImpact: Risk of damage to PCM and other electronic modules.

fixSteps.title: Voltage Check
fixSteps.instruction: Measure charging voltage - if over 15V, alternator is suspect.

fixSteps.title: Replace Alternator
fixSteps.instruction: Install new alternator or regulator.

faq.q: Can over-voltage damage my PCM?
faq.a: Yes - sustained over-voltage is a real risk to all electronics.

faq.q: Is this immediate?
faq.a: Address as soon as possible - don't keep driving with confirmed over-voltage.

title: Stop/Start System Circuit
shortDescription: The stop/start system has detected a circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P2545 indicates a fault in the electrical circuit that commands the stop/start system (auto engine off at stops). The PCM has detected an open, short, or implausible signal.

Diagnosis involves checking harness and the dedicated stop/start button or relay.
safetyImpact: Stop/start feature inoperative; no driving safety issue.

fixSteps.title: Battery Test
fixSteps.instruction: Test main and auxiliary batteries.

fixSteps.title: Harness Check
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect stop/start control wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace stop/start button or weak battery.

faq.q: Why won't my stop/start work?
faq.a: Often an aging auxiliary battery - the system disables itself to protect starter draw.

faq.q: Can I ignore it?
faq.a: Yes - the car still runs; only the efficiency feature is disabled.

title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit / Open
shortDescription: The PCM has detected an open or out-of-range signal in the electric coolant pump control circuit.
fullDescription:
P2600 indicates the engine control module detected an electrical fault in the auxiliary or primary electric coolant pump control circuit. Many modern vehicles use electric coolant pumps to aid warm-up, cool the turbocharger after shutdown, or continue cooling a hybrid system when the engine is off.

When the PCM commands the pump and does not see the expected current draw or voltage feedback, it logs P2600. If left unrepaired, the engine may overheat under load or after a hot shutdown, particularly on turbocharged and hybrid vehicles.
safetyImpact: Potential engine overheating or turbocharger heat soak damage; hybrid battery cooling may also be affected.

causes.cause: Blown coolant pump fuse or relay
Wiring harness open between PCM and pump

fixSteps.title: Scan codes
fixSteps.instruction: Record all codes and freeze-frame data; note coolant temp at the time of fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pump power
fixSteps.instruction: Check fuse and relay for the auxiliary coolant pump. Back-probe connector and measure battery voltage when commanded on.

fixSteps.title: Bench test pump
fixSteps.instruction: Apply 12V directly to pump terminals. If it does not run or runs intermittently, replace the pump.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Drain coolant, remove pump, install new unit, refill and bleed cooling system.

faq.q: Can I drive with P2600?
faq.a: Short trips only. Monitor temperature closely and avoid hard driving until the pump is repaired.

faq.q: Is the electric coolant pump the same as the mechanical water pump?
faq.a: No, it is an auxiliary electric pump that runs independently of the belt-driven water pump.

title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: The coolant pump control circuit is responding but not within expected range or performance.
fullDescription:
The PCM commanded the electric coolant pump and detected that the feedback or current draw is out of the expected range. The pump may run slower than commanded, faster than commanded, or cycle erratically.

On hybrid vehicles this can also affect inverter or battery cooling loops. Continued operation risks overheating components during heavy load or slow-speed driving.
safetyImpact: Engine or hybrid-component overheating possible if pump flow is inadequate.

fixSteps.title: Scan live data
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor commanded vs actual pump duty cycle and current draw with a scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Bleed cooling system
fixSteps.instruction: Perform manufacturer bleed procedure to remove air pockets that can confuse pump feedback.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for corroded pins or chafed wiring that could raise circuit resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: If duty cycle and voltage are correct but flow is not, replace the pump assembly.

faq.q: Will bleeding the system clear the code?
faq.a: Sometimes — trapped air causes false performance codes. Bleed first, then retest.

title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: The coolant pump control circuit voltage is lower than expected.
fullDescription:
When commanded on, the PCM detects that the coolant pump circuit voltage stays pulled low, indicating a short to ground or a PCM driver failure. The pump may run continuously or not respond to PCM commands.

This can overwork the pump, drain the battery at shutdown on vehicles with after-run cooling, or prevent engine warm-up.
safetyImpact: Battery drain and premature pump wear; possible overheating if pump does not respond.
symptoms: Pump runs constantly or not at all

fixSteps.title: Disconnect pump
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the pump and retest. If the low condition clears, the pump is internally shorted.

fixSteps.title: Check wiring for short
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance from the control wire to ground with the connector disconnected and PCM unplugged.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty component
fixSteps.instruction: Repair the shorted wire or replace the pump. Verify PCM driver as a last resort.

faq.q: Why does the pump keep running after shutdown?
faq.a: A shorted low-side control circuit keeps the pump powered even when the PCM commands it off.

title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
shortDescription: The coolant pump control circuit voltage is higher than expected.
fullDescription:
The PCM detects the control circuit voltage stuck high, indicating an open circuit or a short to B+. The pump likely will not run because the driver cannot pull the circuit low to complete the ground path.

This typically means there is a broken wire, open connector, or failed PCM driver. Engine overheating risk rises sharply if the auxiliary pump is required for thermal management.
safetyImpact: Possible engine or turbo overheating since pump cannot be commanded on.

causes.cause: Short to battery voltage on control wire

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check pump connector for bent pins, corrosion, or moisture intrusion.

fixSteps.title: Test control wire
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe the control wire while commanding the pump. Voltage should toggle; if stuck high, test continuity to PCM.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Repair the open wire or replace the connector. If wiring is intact, replace the PCM.

faq.q: Can a blown fuse cause this?
faq.a: A fuse feeding the control circuit or pump power can produce a high-voltage reading, so check fuses first.

title: Camshaft Position Output Circuit/Open
shortDescription: The PCM detected an open condition on the camshaft position output signal line.
fullDescription:
P2614 is set when the PCM's camshaft position output signal, which is provided to other modules such as the transmission controller, is detected as open. This signal helps other modules synchronize with engine events.

A lost cam output signal can cause shifting abnormalities, tachometer glitches in some modules, or loss of certain features that rely on engine position data.
safetyImpact: Potential shifting issues or loss of cruise/start-stop functions.

causes.cause: Open wire between PCM and downstream module

fixSteps.title: Identify downstream consumer
fixSteps.instruction: Reference wiring diagram to find which module receives the cam output signal.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity of the output wire from PCM to receiving module with both disconnected.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Repair any open, or replace the PCM if the driver is confirmed failed.

faq.q: Is this the same as a bad cam sensor?
faq.a: No — this is the PCM's output signal, not the input from the cam sensor.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Stuck On
shortDescription: The transmission pressure control solenoid D is stuck in the energized position.
fullDescription:
P2715 indicates the transmission control module detected that pressure control solenoid D is not releasing when commanded off. Stuck solenoids prevent proper line pressure modulation which can cause firm shifts, slipping clutches, or limp mode.

Contamination in the valve body is the most common cause. Long transmission service intervals and overheating accelerate wear on solenoid bores and seals.
safetyImpact: Harsh shifts and potential clutch damage; vehicle may enter limp mode.

causes.cause: Valve body contamination or stuck solenoid

fixSteps.title: Check fluid
fixSteps.instruction: Verify ATF level, color and smell. Burnt or dark fluid suggests internal wear.

fixSteps.title: Scan TCM data
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor commanded vs actual line pressure and solenoid feedback.

fixSteps.title: Service valve body
fixSteps.instruction: Drop pan, replace filter, inspect valve body and solenoids. Replace solenoid D or entire valve body as needed.

faq.q: Will a fluid flush fix it?
faq.a: Sometimes on early failures, but if the solenoid is physically stuck it must be cleaned or replaced.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Electrical
shortDescription: An electrical fault was detected in the transmission pressure control solenoid D circuit.
fullDescription:
P2716 is a hard electrical fault code indicating the solenoid D circuit resistance, voltage, or current is outside the expected range. This commonly points to a shorted coil, wiring damage, or a failed TCM driver.

Depending on severity the transmission may default to a safe gear or enter limp mode until the fault is cleared.
safetyImpact: Limp mode activation and potential loss of gear selection.

fixSteps.title: Measure solenoid resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With pan down, measure solenoid D resistance. Compare to service spec, typically 3-15 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Inspect internal harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check the pass-through connector and internal harness for chafing or oil intrusion.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid or valve body
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the faulty solenoid or the entire solenoid pack / valve body.

faq.q: Can I reset it and keep driving?
faq.a: Not recommended — the TCM will re-set it and unresolved electrical issues can damage the transmission.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Performance / Stuck Off
shortDescription: Pressure control solenoid E is stuck in the de-energized position or performing poorly.
fullDescription: The TCM commanded solenoid E on but did not see a corresponding change in line pressure or hydraulic response. This points to a solenoid stuck off, a blocked passage, or low fluid delivery. The transmission may slip or hold in a default gear.
safetyImpact: Possible loss of forward motion or harsh shifts.

fixSteps.title: Fluid check
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm proper fluid level and condition.

fixSteps.title: Valve body service
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean valve body, replace solenoid E if stuck.

faq.q: What is solenoid E?
faq.a: It is one of several pressure control solenoids in the valve body that modulate hydraulic pressure for clutches.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Stuck On
shortDescription: Pressure control solenoid E stays energized when it should be off.
fullDescription: Solenoid E is not returning to the off state when commanded, causing persistent line pressure or unwanted clutch engagement. Contaminated ATF and aged valve body components are typical root causes.
safetyImpact: Harsh shifts and possible clutch damage if unaddressed.

fixSteps.title: Fluid and filter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace ATF and filter, inspect pan for debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Replace solenoid E or valve body as needed.

faq.q: Is this safe to drive?
faq.a: Short distances only; continued driving can damage clutches.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage detected on the pressure control solenoid F circuit.
fullDescription: The TCM sees the control circuit for solenoid F pulled low — often a short to ground, a shorted solenoid, or a failed driver. Depending on hydraulic layout the transmission may slip, hold a fixed ratio, or enter limp mode.
safetyImpact: Limp mode and possible loss of higher gears.

fixSteps.title: Resistance check
fixSteps.instruction: Measure solenoid F coil resistance and compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Harness inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect internal wiring between pass-through and solenoid.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Replace solenoid, harness, or valve body as indicated.

faq.q: Can I flash-reset this code?
faq.a: Only after repair; clearing without fixing will trigger immediate re-set.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage detected on the pressure control solenoid F circuit.
fullDescription: The TCM detects the solenoid F control wire stuck at or near system voltage, indicating an open circuit or short to B+. The solenoid cannot be energized, causing drivability problems depending on its hydraulic function.
safetyImpact: Limp mode and loss of certain gear ratios.

fixSteps.title: Inspect external connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check for oil intrusion at the transmission pass-through connector.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Test wire from TCM to solenoid for open.

fixSteps.title: Repair circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Replace damaged connector or internal harness; repair open wire.

faq.q: My external connector is oily — does that matter?
faq.a: Yes. Fluid wicking up the wires corrupts the circuit and is a common cause of open or high faults.

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage detected from transmission fluid temperature sensor B.
fullDescription: The TCM sees the voltage signal from ATF temperature sensor B below the expected range, suggesting a shorted sensor, grounded wiring, or a pegged-hot sensor reading. Incorrect fluid temperature readings can cause inappropriate line pressure, converter clutch strategy, or shift firmness.
safetyImpact: Possible shift harshness and accelerated ATF wear from incorrect cooling strategy.

fixSteps.title: Read sensor value
fixSteps.instruction: Compare scan tool ATF temperature to actual pan temperature with an IR thermometer.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across sensor pins and compare to chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/valve body
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the sensor (often integrated with valve body or TEHCM).

faq.q: Does a wrong ATF temp reading hurt the transmission?
faq.a: Yes — the TCM uses ATF temperature to set line pressure, and wrong values can cause premature wear.

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage detected from transmission fluid temperature sensor B.
fullDescription: The signal from ATF temperature sensor B is at or near reference voltage, indicating an open circuit or pegged-cold reading. The TCM may default to a fixed temperature estimate which can cause delayed torque converter lockup or incorrect line pressure.
safetyImpact: Shift quality may suffer; long-term wear possible.
symptoms: ATF temp stuck at cold value on scan tool

fixSteps.title: Scan and compare
fixSteps.instruction: Check reported ATF temperature vs ambient and engine coolant temp after soak.

fixSteps.title: Check continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Test continuity and reference voltage at sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor or harness
fixSteps.instruction: Replace as needed, including the external connector if fluid-fouled.

faq.q: Will driving cause damage?
faq.a: Short-term driving is usually fine, but persistent wrong temperature readings can cause long-term transmission wear.

title: Transmission Fluid Cooler Control Circuit
shortDescription: A fault has been detected in the transmission fluid cooler control circuit.
fullDescription:
Some transmissions use an electrically controlled ATF cooler bypass valve or electric cooling fan to manage fluid temperature. P2753 indicates the TCM detected an issue in the cooler control circuit — either no response or out-of-range feedback.

Without proper cooling control, ATF temperatures can climb under load, leading to accelerated wear.
safetyImpact: ATF overheating possible under sustained load or towing.

fixSteps.title: Command test
fixSteps.instruction: Use bi-directional scan tool to command cooler bypass or fan and verify activation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring and relay
fixSteps.instruction: Verify relay, fuse and harness continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the solenoid, relay, or fan as indicated.

faq.q: Does this affect engine coolant?
faq.a: No, but some vehicles share a cooler loop — check both systems on overheating complaints.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: The torque converter clutch (TCC) pressure control solenoid is not performing within expected range.
fullDescription:
P2762 indicates the TCM commanded the TCC pressure control solenoid and did not see the expected change in converter clutch slip or apply pressure. Typical causes include worn solenoid, contaminated ATF, or TCC apply/release valve wear.

Symptoms include shudder on light throttle, poor fuel economy, and RPM hunting at cruise.
safetyImpact: Reduced fuel economy and possible TCC shudder under load.

causes.cause: Worn TCC apply valve in valve body

fixSteps.title: Fluid service
fixSteps.instruction: Drain and refill ATF with correct specification fluid; inspect for debris.

fixSteps.title: Sonnax valve test
fixSteps.instruction: On common platforms, test the TCC apply valve bore for wear using a Sonnax vacuum tester.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid/valve body
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the TCC pressure control solenoid or rebuild the valve body with updated parts.

faq.q: Why does the car shudder at 45-55 mph?
faq.a: Classic TCC shudder from worn apply/release circuitry; often fixed with fluid service and updated valve body parts.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit High
shortDescription: The TCC pressure control solenoid circuit is showing excessive voltage.
fullDescription: The TCM detected the TCC pressure control solenoid circuit stuck at high voltage, indicating an open circuit or short to B+. Without control of TCC pressure, the converter may not lock up, causing poor fuel economy and heat buildup.
safetyImpact: Increased ATF temperatures and reduced fuel economy.

fixSteps.title: Coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure the TCC solenoid coil resistance; open reading confirms internal failure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for open or corroded pass-through connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid or harness
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed component and refill ATF.

faq.q: Is this expensive to fix?
faq.a: Cost varies — a standalone solenoid is cheap, but many modern transmissions require valve body replacement.

title: Transmission Range Sensor A Performance
shortDescription: The transmission range sensor A is reporting inconsistent or unexpected gear position data.
fullDescription: P2802 is set when the TCM or PCM sees conflicting information from the transmission range (TR) sensor — for example, reporting two gears simultaneously or jumping between positions. A faulty TR sensor can prevent starting, cause harsh shifts, or disable cruise control.
safetyImpact: Possible no-start, stuck-in-park, or sudden loss of drive; starter interlock may misbehave.

fixSteps.title: Linkage check
fixSteps.instruction: Verify shift cable adjustment and TR sensor alignment to manual valve lever.

fixSteps.title: Live data test
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle through gears with scan tool and watch TR sensor readings for any skipped or duplicated positions.

fixSteps.title: Replace TR sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the sensor and re-adjust linkage to spec.

faq.q: Can the car be towed with this code?
faq.a: Usually yes, but if it won't shift out of park you may need flatbed towing.

title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent signal detected from transmission range sensor A.
fullDescription: The TCM is seeing sporadic dropouts or glitches in the TR sensor A signal. This is frequently caused by loose connectors, chafed wiring, or an internally arcing sensor. Intermittent faults may clear on their own but typically return under vibration or temperature changes.
safetyImpact: Occasional wrong-gear indication and potential starting issues.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: With engine running, wiggle the TR sensor harness while watching scan data for signal changes.

fixSteps.title: Connector service
fixSteps.instruction: Clean and re-seat connector, apply dielectric grease.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring is good, replace the TR sensor.

faq.q: My code keeps coming back only when cold — why?
faq.a: Cold temps shrink connector seals and expose marginal contacts, causing the fault.

title: Transmission Range Sensor B Performance
shortDescription: The secondary transmission range sensor is reporting inconsistent gear data.
fullDescription: Vehicles with redundant range sensing compare sensors A and B. P2806 is set when sensor B's reported position does not agree with sensor A, other inputs, or expected ranges. Shifting, start enable, and reverse lights can all be affected.
safetyImpact: Possible start interlock misbehavior or loss of reverse lights.
symptoms: Reverse lights staying on or off

fixSteps.title: Scan data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare sensor A and B readings through each gear.

fixSteps.title: Realign sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor mounting alignment per service spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace TR sensor B if signal does not track correctly.

faq.q: Why are there two range sensors?
faq.a: Redundancy lets the TCM detect sensor failures and protect against unintended drive-away conditions.

title: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent or erratic signal from transmission range sensor B.
fullDescription: Similar to P2803 but for the secondary range sensor, P2807 is set when the TCM sees intermittent drops or glitches in the sensor B signal. Common causes are connector corrosion and harness damage near the transmission.
safetyImpact: Occasional shifting or indicator anomalies.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Observe sensor B reading while manipulating wiring.

fixSteps.title: Service connector
fixSteps.instruction: Clean pins and ensure secure seating.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring is good, replace sensor B.

faq.q: Can I clear it and ignore it?
faq.a: Intermittent faults tend to return — diagnose before they progress to hard faults.

title: Gear Selection Signal Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: A fault has been detected in the manual gear selection signal circuit.
fullDescription: Many modern transmissions allow paddle-shift or manual +/- gear selection through a dedicated switch or bus message. P2825 indicates the TCM is not seeing valid selection signals, which can disable manumatic mode and keep the transmission in fully automatic operation.
safetyImpact: No safety impact; manual shift mode may be unavailable.

causes.cause: CAN bus message missing from steering wheel module

fixSteps.title: Test switches
fixSteps.instruction: Check switch resistance or bus message with scan tool to verify correct input.

fixSteps.title: Inspect clock spring
fixSteps.instruction: On steering-wheel-mounted paddles, inspect the clock spring for continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch or module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace paddle assembly, shift selector, or related module.

faq.q: Does this affect normal driving?
faq.a: No — the transmission continues to shift automatically; only the manual override is lost.

title: Transfer Case Clutch Pressure Control Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: A fault has been detected in the electronic transfer case clutch pressure control circuit.
fullDescription:
On electronically controlled AWD/4WD systems, the transfer case uses a clutch actuator to vary torque split. P2856 is set when the control module cannot properly modulate the clutch pressure, typically due to actuator motor failure or wiring problems.

The vehicle may revert to a default torque split or, in severe cases, disable AWD until repaired.
safetyImpact: Reduced AWD performance and potential loss of traction assistance.

fixSteps.title: Scan AWD module
fixSteps.instruction: Read codes from the transfer case control module; check actuator commanded vs actual position.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check harness routing for damage or connector corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the clutch actuator/encoder motor and relearn per service procedure.

faq.q: Is AWD still safe to use?
faq.a: Use caution — if the system is compromised, avoid heavy off-road use until repaired.

title: Shift Fork Position Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Shift fork position sensor is reporting out-of-range performance data.
fullDescription:
Dual-clutch and many automated manual transmissions use position sensors on the shift forks to verify engagement. P2901 is set when the shift fork position is not changing as commanded or is drifting outside expected range.

Common on DCTs and AMTs, this code can cause harsh engagement, failed shifts, or limp mode.
safetyImpact: Failed shifts or limp mode operation.

fixSteps.title: Read module data
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory-level scan tool to view actual fork positions.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fork mechanism
fixSteps.instruction: If accessible, inspect for wear or contamination.

fixSteps.title: Replace mechatronic/sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Often requires replacing the mechatronic unit and re-adapting.

faq.q: Can I drive with P2901?
faq.a: Not recommended — failed shifts can strand the vehicle.

title: Shift Fork C Position Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage detected from the shift fork C position sensor.
fullDescription: The TCM sees the shift fork C position signal pulled low, indicating a short to ground, a failed sensor, or damaged wiring. Dual-clutch and automated manual transmissions rely on these sensors to confirm engagement, so a low signal typically forces limp mode.
safetyImpact: Limp mode and possible no-drive condition.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in neutral or fixed gear

fixSteps.title: Read mechatronic data
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory tool to read fork C sensor voltage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect internal mechatronic harness for damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace mechatronic
fixSteps.instruction: Replace mechatronic unit; relearn adaptations.

faq.q: Does a DCT software update help?
faq.a: Sometimes — manufacturers release mechatronic flashes for known fork sensor sensitivity; check TSBs first.

title: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage detected on the primary control circuit of ignition coil A (cylinder 1).
fullDescription:
The PCM drives ignition coils via a low-side switch (IGBT). P2300 indicates the primary control wire for coil A is stuck low, suggesting a shorted coil driver, shorted wiring, or a failed IGBT inside the coil pack.

Resulting symptoms include cylinder 1 misfires and possible PCM damage if left unrepaired.
safetyImpact: Severe misfire possible; unburnt fuel may damage the catalytic converter.

fixSteps.title: Swap coil
fixSteps.instruction: Swap coil 1 with another cylinder; if the fault moves, replace the coil.

fixSteps.title: Check wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the primary control wire for shorts to ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil/PCM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the ignition coil or, rarely, the PCM driver.

faq.q: Can a bad coil damage the PCM?
faq.a: Yes — a shorted coil primary can take out the PCM ignition driver.

title: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage detected on the primary control circuit of ignition coil A.
fullDescription: The PCM sees the coil A primary wire stuck high, indicating an open circuit or short to B+. The cylinder will not fire and will misfire on every cycle.
safetyImpact: Severe misfire and catalyst damage risk.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check coil connector and wiring for breaks.

fixSteps.title: Swap coil test
fixSteps.instruction: Swap with another cylinder and re-scan.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil/wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil or repair harness as needed.

faq.q: Can I drive home with it?
faq.a: Only if absolutely necessary — running with a dead cylinder fouls the catalyst quickly.

title: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on ignition coil B primary control circuit (cylinder 2).
fullDescription: Similar to P2300 but for cylinder 2. The PCM detects a short or stuck-low condition on coil B's primary control line. Common causes include a shorted coil or wiring damage.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 2 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Swap test
fixSteps.instruction: Swap coil 2 with another; if code follows, replace coil.

fixSteps.title: Wiring check
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect primary wiring for short.

faq.q: Why only coil B?
faq.a: Each coil has its own driver and wiring — failures are usually localized.

title: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on ignition coil B primary control circuit.
fullDescription: An open or stuck-high condition on the coil B primary. The PCM cannot drive the coil, causing cylinder 2 misfire.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 2 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Connector check
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect coil connector and wiring for breaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil or repair open wire.

faq.q: Is this the same as a spark plug problem?
faq.a: No — this is the coil primary circuit, not the secondary spark.

title: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on ignition coil C primary control circuit (cylinder 3).
fullDescription: Low/stuck-low condition on cylinder 3 ignition coil primary. Frequently a shorted coil or wiring short to ground.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 3 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Swap test
fixSteps.instruction: Move coil 3 to a different cylinder and watch for code migration.

fixSteps.title: Wiring inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Check primary wire for shorts.

faq.q: Do I need to replace all coils?
faq.a: Not necessarily — replace the failed coil first, though aged sets often fail progressively.

title: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on ignition coil C primary control circuit.
fullDescription: Open or stuck-high on the cylinder 3 coil primary. Cylinder cannot fire.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 3 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector and wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil if primary reads open.

faq.q: Will new spark plugs help?
faq.a: Not for this code — fix the coil or wiring first.

title: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on ignition coil D primary control circuit (cylinder 4).
fullDescription: Short or stuck-low on cylinder 4 coil primary.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 4 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Swap coil
fixSteps.instruction: Move coil to another cylinder to confirm fault.

fixSteps.title: Wiring test
fixSteps.instruction: Check primary wire for short to ground.

faq.q: How long can the coil last after this code?
faq.a: Not long — a shorted coil can fail completely at any time.

title: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on ignition coil D primary control circuit.
fullDescription: Open or stuck-high on cylinder 4 coil primary; cylinder cannot fire.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 4 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector and wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil if primary reads open.

faq.q: Is this ignition or fuel related?
faq.a: Ignition — specifically the coil primary driver circuit.

title: Ignition Coil E Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on ignition coil E primary control circuit (cylinder 5).
fullDescription: Short or stuck-low on cylinder 5 coil primary.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 5 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Swap test
fixSteps.instruction: Move coil 5 and rescan.

fixSteps.title: Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check primary wiring.

faq.q: Is this common on inline-6 engines?
faq.a: Yes, cylinders 5 and 6 coils on inline engines often accumulate heat damage.

title: Ignition Coil E Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on ignition coil E primary control circuit.
fullDescription: Open or stuck-high on cylinder 5 coil primary; cylinder cannot fire.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 5 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector and wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil and inspect connector.

faq.q: Can heat from the exhaust kill coils?
faq.a: Yes, heat soak is a major cause of coil primary open failures.

title: Ignition Coil F Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on ignition coil F primary control circuit (cylinder 6).
fullDescription: Short or stuck-low on cylinder 6 coil primary.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 6 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Swap test
fixSteps.instruction: Relocate coil 6 and rescan.

fixSteps.title: Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for short to ground.

faq.q: Should I replace plugs at the same time?
faq.a: It is a good idea if plugs are aged — fouled plugs stress coils.

title: Ignition Coil F Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on ignition coil F primary control circuit.
fullDescription: Open or stuck-high on cylinder 6 coil primary; cylinder cannot fire.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 6 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector and wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil; verify fix.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep driving?
faq.a: Not recommended — misfires damage the catalyst quickly.

title: Ignition Coil G Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on ignition coil G primary control circuit (cylinder 7).
fullDescription: Short or stuck-low on cylinder 7 coil primary. Found on V8 and some V10 engines.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 7 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Swap test
fixSteps.instruction: Relocate coil 7 and verify.

fixSteps.title: Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check primary wire for ground short.

faq.q: Why are V8 rear coils so often failed?
faq.a: Heat soak and limited airflow make rear-bank coils fail first.

title: Ignition Coil G Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on ignition coil G primary control circuit.
fullDescription: Open or stuck-high on cylinder 7 coil primary.
safetyImpact: Cylinder 7 misfire; catalyst damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector and wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil; confirm fix.

faq.q: Should I replace both rear-bank coils?
faq.a: If the others are the original age, preventative replacement is reasonable.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
shortDescription: Bank 2 diesel particulate filter is not trapping soot effectively.
fullDescription:
P2003 is set when the PCM determines that the DPF on bank 2 is not meeting its required efficiency. Differential pressure sensors across the filter help the PCM evaluate both flow and soot load.

Reduced efficiency can indicate a cracked or failed substrate, a stuck open EGR valve, or sensor issues.
safetyImpact: Potential limp mode and emissions non-compliance.

fixSteps.title: Scan data
fixSteps.instruction: Read DPF soot load and differential pressure sensor values.

fixSteps.title: Inspect filter
fixSteps.instruction: Check for cracks, melting, or damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace DPF or sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace DPF or sensor as indicated and complete a forced regen.

faq.q: Can a cleaning service save the DPF?
faq.a: Often yes, unless the substrate is cracked or melted — then replacement is required.

title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open Bank 2
shortDescription: Intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 2 is stuck in the open position.
fullDescription: Many engines use intake runner flaps to optimize airflow at different RPMs. P2005 indicates the bank 2 runner is stuck open, resulting in poor low-end torque and rough idle. Common causes are carbon buildup, broken actuator linkage, or failed motor/solenoid.
safetyImpact: Reduced low-speed performance and fuel economy.

fixSteps.title: Visual inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Look at the IMRC linkage while cycling the actuator.

fixSteps.title: Actuator test
fixSteps.instruction: Command the actuator with a scan tool or apply vacuum/electric signal.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clean carbon buildup or replace the IMRC actuator/linkage.

faq.q: Is this a common problem?
faq.a: Yes — especially on direct-injection engines with significant carbon buildup on the intake flaps.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Below Minimum Position
shortDescription: Throttle plate is stuck closed below the learned minimum position.
fullDescription:
The PCM has detected that the electronic throttle plate cannot move above its minimum learned position even when commanded to open. This results in a no-start, stall, or limp-home condition.

Common causes include carbon buildup binding the throttle plate, a failed throttle body motor, broken return spring, or wiring/connector damage to the throttle body actuator.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may not start or may stall in traffic. Forced-idle limp mode reduces controllability.

fixSteps.title: Scan and freeze-frame
fixSteps.instruction: Read codes and freeze-frame data. Inspect throttle position values at key-on.

fixSteps.title: Inspect throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Remove intake duct and check for heavy carbon. Clean with throttle body cleaner if dirty.

fixSteps.title: Test actuator motor
fixSteps.instruction: Bidirectionally command the throttle and verify movement; check motor resistance per spec.

fixSteps.title: Relearn idle
fixSteps.instruction: Perform throttle relearn procedure after cleaning or replacement.

faq.q: Can I just clean the throttle body?
faq.a: Often yes - heavy carbon is the most common cause and a thorough cleaning with relearn fixes many cases.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Above Maximum Position
shortDescription: Throttle plate is stuck open above its maximum learned position.
fullDescription:
The PCM detects the throttle plate cannot return to or below its maximum operational position. This causes uncontrolled high idle and may force the engine into fail-safe mode.

Likely culprits are a binding throttle linkage, broken/weak closing spring, debris under the plate, or a failed actuator motor.
safetyImpact: Uncontrolled high idle can cause unintended acceleration risk; vehicle enters limp mode.

causes.cause: Debris or carbon under throttle plate

fixSteps.title: Inspect throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Visually check plate movement and look for debris/carbon.

fixSteps.title: Clean throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Clean plate and bore with throttle body cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Replace if mechanically failed
fixSteps.instruction: Replace throttle body assembly if motor or spring is faulty.

fixSteps.title: Idle relearn
fixSteps.instruction: Perform idle relearn with scan tool.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive?
faq.a: No - uncontrolled idle and limp mode warrant immediate diagnosis.

title: ETC Throttle Position Sensor Minimum Stop Performance
shortDescription: TPS minimum-stop value is out of expected range during learn.
fullDescription:
During the throttle learn cycle, the PCM could not establish a valid minimum-stop position from the throttle position sensor. The learned closed-throttle reference is corrupted or out of spec.

Causes include a worn throttle body, faulty TPS, intake leaks affecting idle, or improper learn procedure after disconnecting the battery.
safetyImpact: Idle may be unstable; limp mode possible.

fixSteps.title: Perform idle/throttle relearn
fixSteps.instruction: Run OEM relearn procedure with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Check for vacuum leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Smoke-test intake.

fixSteps.title: Replace throttle body if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If learn fails repeatedly, replace throttle body.

faq.q: Do I need a scan tool?
faq.a: Yes - most modern vehicles require an electronic relearn that cannot be done by disconnecting the battery alone.

title: ETC Throttle Position Sensor Minimum Stop Performance Bank 2
shortDescription: Bank 2 throttle minimum-stop reference invalid.
fullDescription: On engines with two throttle bodies (V engines with bank-specific control), the PCM could not validate the minimum-stop position for bank 2. Causes mirror P2116 but apply to the second throttle body.
safetyImpact: Bank 2 idle and torque control degraded.

fixSteps.title: Inspect bank 2 throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Clean and inspect.

fixSteps.title: Relearn
fixSteps.instruction: Run scan-tool relearn for both banks.

faq.q: Common on V engines?
faq.a: Yes - dual-throttle V engines (some BMW/Audi) trip this when bank 2 throttle sync drifts.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit
shortDescription: General electrical fault in pedal position sensor E circuit.
fullDescription:
The PCM detected an out-of-range condition or open in the accelerator pedal position sensor E circuit. APP sensors typically have two or three independent channels for redundancy.

Causes include a failed pedal assembly, damaged harness, poor ground, or PCM input fault.
safetyImpact: Reduced engine power - throttle response disabled until fault clears.

fixSteps.title: Scan and read APP signals
fixSteps.instruction: Live-data both APP channels.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector and harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check pins, voltage, and ground at pedal sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace pedal assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Replace APP sensor/pedal if fault confirmed.

faq.q: Can I drive in this state?
faq.a: Only short distances at low speed - the vehicle will be in reduced-power mode.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor E Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: APP sensor E reading out of expected range vs. pedal position.
fullDescription:
The signal from APP sensor channel E does not track properly with pedal travel. May be intermittent or appear only at certain pedal angles.

Likely caused by a worn/contaminated pedal sensor, internal short, or signal-wire chafing.
safetyImpact: Reduced power; possible unintended throttle behavior.

fixSteps.title: Graph APP signals through full pedal travel
fixSteps.instruction: Watch for dropouts.

fixSteps.title: Replace pedal
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if signal scatter confirmed.

faq.q: Will cleaning the pedal help?
faq.a: No - APP sensors are sealed; replace as a unit.

title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
shortDescription: Upstream NOx sensor reading out of expected range.
fullDescription:
The bank 1 NOx sensor is reporting values inconsistent with engine operating conditions, expected exhaust temperature, or fuel/SCR injection state. Common on diesel SCR systems and lean-burn gasoline engines.

Common causes are sensor contamination from soot/fuel, damaged heater element, exhaust leaks before the sensor, or wiring faults.
safetyImpact: Increased NOx emissions; SCR strategy may go open-loop. Possible derate on diesels.

fixSteps.title: Read live NOx data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare upstream vs. downstream NOx sensor values across operating range.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Check for leaks ahead of sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace NOx sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor and clear adaptations.

faq.q: Are NOx sensors expensive?
faq.a: Yes - typically $200-$700+ for the part alone.

title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent Bank 1
shortDescription: Intermittent fault detected in bank 1 NOx sensor signal.
fullDescription: Signal from the bank 1 NOx sensor drops out or spikes intermittently. Often caused by loose connectors, vibration-induced wiring issues, or a failing sensor heater.
safetyImpact: Inconsistent SCR control; emissions may exceed limits.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test connector
fixSteps.instruction: Flex harness while watching live data.

fixSteps.title: Repair/replace as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Re-pin or replace connector; replace sensor if internal.

faq.q: Can I clean a NOx sensor?
faq.a: No - the ceramic element is sensitive and not cleanable.

title: Barometric Pressure Circuit
shortDescription: Barometric pressure (BARO) signal out of range.
fullDescription:
The PCM uses a barometric pressure value (sometimes from a dedicated sensor, sometimes inferred from MAP at key-on) to compensate fueling and timing for altitude. P2226 sets when the BARO value is outside expected range.

Causes include a failing MAP/BARO sensor, vacuum leak at sensor port, or PCM input fault.
safetyImpact: Minor driveability issues at altitude; emissions may rise.

fixSteps.title: Read BARO at key-on
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to known altitude-corrected value.

fixSteps.title: Replace MAP/BARO sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor.

faq.q: Is this dangerous?
faq.a: No - generally a low-severity emissions code.

title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
shortDescription: Wide-band O2 sensor virtual-ground reference low on bank 1.
fullDescription:
Wide-band air/fuel sensors use a negative voltage (virtual ground) reference. P2252 indicates the negative reference circuit is below specification for bank 1 sensor 1.

Most commonly the AFR sensor itself or its harness/connector.
safetyImpact: Closed-loop fuel control degraded; emissions and economy worsen.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor wiring and connector
fixSteps.instruction: Visual and DMM check.

fixSteps.title: Replace AFR sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor; clear adaptations.

faq.q: Is the AFR sensor the same as a regular O2?
faq.a: No - it has more wires and reads air/fuel ratio over a wider range.

title: Turbo/Super Charger Bypass Valve - Mechanical
shortDescription: Boost bypass (blow-off/diverter) valve mechanically stuck or leaking.
fullDescription:
The PCM detects boost levels inconsistent with bypass-valve commands. The diverter/blow-off valve may be stuck open, leaking, or its diaphragm torn.

Causes include diaphragm rupture, stuck plunger, or vacuum-line failure to the valve.
safetyImpact: Reduced boost; possible compressor surge.

fixSteps.title: Inspect diverter valve and lines
fixSteps.instruction: Check diaphragm and vacuum hose integrity.

fixSteps.title: Replace diverter valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install new bypass/diverter valve.

faq.q: Will an aftermarket BOV work?
faq.a: Often yes for tuning, but stock-style is usually best for emissions compliance.

title: Air Flow Restriction / MAF Sensor Performance
shortDescription: Detected restriction in air intake or MAF performance issue.
fullDescription:
The PCM has determined that airflow into the engine is below expected for the throttle/RPM operating point. Often a clogged air filter, collapsed intake duct, or contaminated MAF sensor.

Diesel engines may set this with a clogged DPF or intake throttle issue.
safetyImpact: Reduced power; possible smoke on diesel.

fixSteps.title: Inspect air filter and ducting
fixSteps.instruction: Replace filter; check for collapsed/torn duct.

fixSteps.title: Clean MAF
fixSteps.instruction: Use MAF-safe cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Check intake throttle (diesel)
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect intake throttle plate for soot/sticking.

faq.q: Easy to fix?
faq.a: Usually yes - start with the cheapest items: filter and MAF cleaning.

title: Ignition Coil C Secondary Circuit
shortDescription: Secondary ignition fault detected in coil C circuit.
fullDescription:
The PCM detected an abnormality in the high-voltage secondary side of ignition coil C, typically through ion-current sensing or misfire feedback. Causes include a failing coil, fouled spark plug, or arcing boot.

Replacing the spark plug, coil, and boot together for that cylinder is often the fix.
safetyImpact: Misfire on the affected cylinder; potential catalyst damage.

fixSteps.title: Identify cylinder
fixSteps.instruction: Determine which cylinder coil C maps to per service info.

fixSteps.title: Swap coil to next cylinder
fixSteps.instruction: If misfire follows, replace coil.

fixSteps.title: Replace plug and boot
fixSteps.instruction: Install new spark plug and boot.

faq.q: Should I replace all coils?
faq.a: Not required, but if vehicle has high mileage and original coils, all-at-once replacement saves labor down the road.

title: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Coil D primary control circuit voltage below threshold.
fullDescription:
The PCM detected the primary driver circuit for ignition coil D is below expected voltage, typically indicating a short to ground or open driver in the PCM/ICM.

Check wiring before replacing the PCM.
safetyImpact: Cylinder D misfire; reduced power.

causes.cause: Short to ground in coil control wire

fixSteps.title: Test coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Verify primary winding spec.

fixSteps.title: Check coil control wire
fixSteps.instruction: Look for short to ground or chafe.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Install new coil if winding faulty.

faq.q: Could it be the PCM?
faq.a: Rarely - check wiring and coil first.

title: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit High
shortDescription: Coil D primary control circuit voltage above threshold.
fullDescription: Indicates an open or short-to-power on the primary control side of coil D. Often a broken connector pin, corroded contact, or wiring damage.
safetyImpact: Cylinder misfire.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check pins and lock.

fixSteps.title: Repair wire/connector
fixSteps.instruction: Re-pin or splice.

faq.q: Will a new coil fix it?
faq.a: Sometimes, but check wiring first to avoid replacing parts unnecessarily.

title: Ignition Coil D Secondary Circuit
shortDescription: Secondary fault on coil D - typically misfire feedback.
fullDescription: The PCM has detected an abnormal secondary circuit on coil D. Often this code is paired with a P0354 misfire on the corresponding cylinder.
safetyImpact: Catalyst damage risk during sustained misfire.

fixSteps.title: Replace plug/boot/coil for cyl D
fixSteps.instruction: Standard misfire trio replacement.

faq.q: Is a flashing MIL serious?
faq.a: Yes - flashing MIL indicates active misfire that can damage the catalytic converter.

title: Ignition Coil E Primary Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Coil E primary driver voltage low.
fullDescription: Same diagnostic family as P2316 but for coil E. Indicates short to ground or shorted coil primary winding.
safetyImpact: Misfire on cylinder E.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose coil and wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Standard primary-circuit diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Install new coil if shorted.

faq.q: Can a single bad coil affect others?
faq.a: A shorted coil can blow PCM drivers, so diagnose promptly.

title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: EVAP leak detection pump sense input out of range.
fullDescription:
Some vehicles use an electric leak-detection pump (LDP) to pressurize the EVAP system and confirm integrity. P2406 indicates the pump's pressure-sense feedback is outside expected range.

Common on older European vehicles; causes include a stuck LDP diaphragm, leaking hose, or failed sense circuit.
safetyImpact: EVAP monitor will not run; emissions inspection failure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect LDP and hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Check pump for diaphragm tear and hoses for cracks.

fixSteps.title: Replace LDP
fixSteps.instruction: Install new leak-detection pump.

faq.q: Will it cause a drivability issue?
faq.a: No - EVAP faults rarely affect drivability.

title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent fault in LDP sense circuit.
fullDescription: An intermittent open or short in the leak detection pump's pressure-sense circuit. Often connector related.
safetyImpact: Periodic MIL; emissions monitor incomplete.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Watch live data while flexing harness.

fixSteps.title: Repair connector or harness
fixSteps.instruction: Re-pin/splice as needed.

faq.q: Is it safe to ignore?
faq.a: Drives fine, but you will fail emissions until repaired.

title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
shortDescription: Upstream O2 sensor not seeing valid exhaust sample.
fullDescription:
The PCM determined the upstream O2 sensor cannot detect a representative exhaust sample - typically due to an exhaust leak ahead of the sensor, missing/loose sensor, or contamination.

Fix exhaust leaks first.
safetyImpact: Closed-loop fueling impaired; emissions rise.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust manifold and gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Look/listen for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Repair leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Replace gasket or weld leak as needed.

faq.q: Will a new O2 sensor fix it?
faq.a: Not if the underlying issue is an exhaust leak.

title: EVAP Vent Solenoid Valve Stuck Open
shortDescription: EVAP canister vent valve stuck in open position.
fullDescription:
The PCM cannot achieve required EVAP system vacuum because the canister vent valve will not seal closed. Common causes are a stuck/contaminated valve or a damaged spring.

Located near the canister at the rear of many vehicles - often exposed to road debris.
safetyImpact: EVAP monitor incomplete; possible fuel odor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect vent valve
fixSteps.instruction: Locate at canister; check for contamination.

fixSteps.title: Replace vent valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install new vent solenoid.

faq.q: Common on trucks?
faq.a: Yes - exposed underbody location collects dirt and water.

title: EVAP Vent Valve Stuck Closed
shortDescription: EVAP vent valve stuck closed - cannot vent canister.
fullDescription: The vent valve fails to open during normal operation, blocking atmospheric venting of the EVAP canister. Tank pressure may build during refueling, causing slow-fill.
safetyImpact: Slow refueling complaint; MIL on.

fixSteps.title: Replace vent valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install new vent solenoid.

faq.q: Why does the pump click off?
faq.a: Tank pressure can't escape, so the pump nozzle senses backpressure.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: PCM power relay feedback signal out of range.
fullDescription: The PCM monitors its own main power-relay feedback. P2510 sets when this sense voltage stays out of expected range during run/key-off cycles. Causes include a sticking relay, blown fuse, or wiring fault.
safetyImpact: Possible no-start, intermittent power loss.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCM main relay
fixSteps.instruction: Swap with known good relay.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for chafe and corrosion.

faq.q: Easy DIY?
faq.a: Yes - swapping a relay is one of the simplest fixes.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent fault on PCM power relay sense.
fullDescription: Same diagnostic family as P2510 but the fault is intermittent - typically corroded relay contacts or vibration-sensitive wiring.
safetyImpact: Random stall; intermittent no-start.

fixSteps.title: Replace relay and inspect socket
fixSteps.instruction: Look for melting/corrosion.

faq.q: Should I replace the PCM?
faq.a: No - check the relay and wiring first; PCM failure is rare.

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
shortDescription: Secondary A/C pressure sensor input above expected range.
fullDescription: On systems with two A/C pressure sensors, the secondary (B) sensor reads above range. Causes include sensor failure, wiring short to power, or genuinely overpressure refrigerant.
safetyImpact: A/C may be disabled; engine load and fan operation affected.

fixSteps.title: Read live A/C pressures
fixSteps.instruction: Compare scan-tool to manifold gauge.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new pressure sensor (often Schrader-style, no recovery needed).

faq.q: Do I need to recover refrigerant?
faq.a: Usually not - most pressure sensors mount on Schrader valves.

title: Cooling Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Electric cooling fan tach feedback out of expected range.
fullDescription: Modern variable-speed electric fans report tachometer feedback to the PCM. P2615 indicates the reported fan speed does not match commanded duty cycle - possibly a stuck fan, failed brushless module, or wiring fault.
safetyImpact: Risk of overheating in traffic.

fixSteps.title: Command fan with scan tool
fixSteps.instruction: Verify response across duty cycles.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fan module.

faq.q: Can I drive it?
faq.a: Only with great care; pull over if temps rise.

title: Throttle Position Output Circuit
shortDescription: PCM-to-other-module TPS output circuit fault.
fullDescription: The PCM transmits a throttle position output signal to another module (often the TCM). P2620 sets when that output cannot be verified - check related module wiring or PCM driver.
safetyImpact: Affects transmission shift quality and traction control.

causes.cause: Open or short on output circuit

fixSteps.title: Probe TPS output wire at TCM
fixSteps.instruction: Verify continuity and signal.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Repair open/short.

faq.q: Will it disable the transmission?
faq.a: Possibly - some vehicles enter limp mode until repaired.

title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A
shortDescription: Generator/alternator torque feedback fault.
fullDescription: Modern smart-charging systems report alternator electrical torque to the PCM for fuel/idle compensation. P2637 indicates the feedback signal is missing or out of range - often a LIN/serial communication fault to the alternator.
safetyImpact: Charging strategy degraded; idle quality may suffer.

fixSteps.title: Check LIN/communication wire
fixSteps.instruction: Probe alternator data line.

fixSteps.title: Replace alternator
fixSteps.instruction: Install OE-spec smart alternator.

faq.q: Will a generic alternator work?
faq.a: Only if it supports the OE communication protocol; otherwise use OE.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent fault on transmission pressure solenoid F.
fullDescription: An intermittent open or short detected on the F pressure-control solenoid in the transmission. Internal harness or contaminated valve body are common.
safetyImpact: Harsh or delayed shifts; possible limp mode.

fixSteps.title: Inspect internal harness
fixSteps.instruction: Drop pan; inspect connector and harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid pack/valve body
fixSteps.instruction: Per manufacturer service info.

faq.q: Will fluid changes help?
faq.a: Sometimes - fresh fluid and a new filter may resolve borderline cases.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Stuck Off
shortDescription: Trans pressure solenoid C stuck in de-energized state.
fullDescription: Solenoid C in the transmission valve body has stopped responding to commands - typically stuck off due to debris or electrical failure. Causes shift quality and ratio errors depending on which clutch it controls.
safetyImpact: Possible neutral / no-shift condition; limp mode.

fixSteps.title: Service trans fluid and inspect pan
fixSteps.instruction: Look for metal/debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid/valve body
fixSteps.instruction: Install new solenoid pack.

faq.q: Could the transmission be done?
faq.a: If metal contamination is severe, internal damage is likely - consult a trans specialist.
